immigration.nri_angle: Simpler Indian visa paperwork for foreign-national relatives, spouses and friends of the diaspora planning trips to India.

immigration.title: Survey: Most Microsoft India Staff Report Hikes Of Five Percent Or Less
immigration.excerpt: A Blind survey of 2,178 India-based professionals found 91% of Microsoft respondents reporting hikes of 5% or less — self-reported figures that arrive alongside a voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees.
immigration.image_caption: An aerial view shows Microsoft's West Campus in Redmond, Washington. A Blind survey found 91% of Microsoft India respondents received pay hikes of 5% or less this year.
immigration.nri_angle: For Indian tech workers in India and the diaspora, the survey captures pay anxiety arriving at the same time as a large voluntary exit offer at one of the sector's biggest employers.

immigration.title: UK Doubles Settlement Wait to Ten Years, Keeps Five-Year Route for Care Workers
immigration.excerpt: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's earned-settlement plan doubles the standard ILR wait from five years to ten, applied retrospectively — but care workers earning at least £25,000 who met their visa conditions, higher earners, and many public sector workers keep a five-year route.
immigration.image_caption: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood leaves 10 Downing Street in London. The government plans to double the qualifying wait for permanent settlement to ten years, while care workers keep a five-year route if they meet visa and earnings conditions.
immigration.nri_angle: Indians are one of the largest groups on UK work and health and care visas, so the doubled ten-year default — and the care-worker and salary carve-outs — directly change settlement timelines for thousands of Indian families in Britain.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian IT Stocks Shrug Off Wall Street Rout as Nifty IT Rises 2%

carousel.title: India Rebased Its GDP, but Rs 34.5 Lakh Crore of Women's Work Counts for Nothing
carousel.excerpt: A ministry-backed study values women's unpaid domestic and care work at up to Rs 34.5 lakh crore — an estimated 15-17% of GDP depending on the wage used — yet the February 2026 rebasing still leaves it outside the accounts.
